label: FICTIONAL lore. Nothing here describes the real universe.

history: The transmissions are built from a layered code. The simplest layer is a counting system with a base the senders seem to have chosen for its symmetry.
A second layer records what looks like a long period of isolation, followed by a deliberate decision to listen rather than broadcast.
The third layer describes a catastrophe that nearly ended their civilization and the archive they built afterwards so it would never be forgotten.
The deepest layer is an invitation: a list of questions, addressed to whoever answers.
tech: Their messages describe a method for filtering noise out of very faint signals.
They record a way to store information in stable atomic arrangements.

history: The signal is a repeating carrier with a slow modulation. Decoding it shows a counting sequence and nothing more, so far.
Long-baseline comparison shows the modulation changes once every few thousand years, as if an automatic system updated the message.
The updates are small corrections, as if the source records the drift of its own clocks and stars.
The final decoded layer is a list of coordinates that match no star we know. They may be places the senders once lived.
tech: The carrier is stabilised in a way our oscillators cannot match.
The sender corrects for stellar motion automatically.

history: The echoes contain a structured preamble that repeats, as if testing whether a listener understands the basic rules.
Subsequent layers show the senders answering only when a message follows their rules exactly. They seem careful.
The records describe past contact that went badly, and a decision to share little until trust is established.
The deepest layer is a short, polite refusal to share more now, and an offer to continue the exchange slowly.
tech: The senders encode messages so that only a listener who has followed the preamble can read them.
Their echoes are shaped to carry as little energy as possible.
